sections.content:
Population change in Barking and Dagenham in 2032

The population in Barking and Dagenham is projected to increase from 220,039 people in 2022 to 229,454 people in 2032.

Despite an overall increase in the population, there is projected to be a fall in net internal migration, which will decrease the population by 39,435 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Barking and Dagenham
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Barking and Dagenham, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 18,547, with 31,807 births and 13,260 deaths in Barking and Dagenham between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Barking and Dagenham by 8.4%, compared with an increase of 6.0% in London and an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 39,435, with 163,520 people moving to the area and 202,954 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Barking and Dagenham by 17.9%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 1,101, with 1,561 people moving to the area and 2,662 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Barking and Dagenham by 0.5%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 31,299, with 57,192 people moving to the area and 25,893 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Barking and Dagenham by 14.2%, compared with an increase of 14.7% in London and an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Barking and Dagenham in 2032

The median age in Barking and Dagenham is projected to rise from 33 years in 2022 to 34 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 9% of the population in Barking and Dagenham are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 8% in 2022.

sections.title: The 0 to 9 age group are set to see the largest change in Barking and Dagenham between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Barking and Dagenham is projected to stay the same, at around 69%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to stay around the same, at 123 in 2032 compared with 124 in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Barking and Dagenham?

In 2032, 26% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 30% in 2022.

This is above average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Barking and Dagenham between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 12% to 10%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 11% to 10%
